    13  This file defines the predictable σ-algebra associated to a filtration, as well as the

    16  
    17  ## Main definitions
    18  
    19  * `Filtration.predictable` : The predictable σ-algebra associated to a filtration.
    20  * `IsStronglyPredictable` : A process is predictable if it is measurable with respect to the
    21    predictable σ-algebra.
    22  
    23  ## Main results
    24  
    25  * `IsStronglyPredictable.isStronglyProgressive` : A predictable process is progressively measurable.
    26  * `IsStronglyPredictable.iff_measurable_add_one` : `u` is a discrete predictable process iff
    27    `u (n + 1)` is `𝓕 n`-measurable and `u 0` is `𝓕 0`-measurable.
    28

    53    MeasurableSpace.generateFrom <|

    55      {s | ∃ i A, MeasurableSet[𝓕 i] A ∧ s = Set.Ioi i ×ˢ A}
    56  
    57  end Filtration

    60      {𝓕 : Filtration ι m} {s : Set Ω} (hs : MeasurableSet[𝓕 ⊥] s) :

    62    MeasurableSpace.measurableSet_generateFrom <| Or.inl ⟨s, hs, rfl⟩
    63

    66      MeasurableSet[𝓕.predictable] <| Set.Ioi i ×ˢ s :=

    68

    70  σ-algebra. -/
    71  lemma measurableSet_predictable_Ioc_prod [LinearOrder ι] [OrderBot ι]
    72      {𝓕 : Filtration ι m} (i j : ι) {s : Set Ω} (hs : MeasurableSet[𝓕 i] s) :
    73      MeasurableSet[𝓕.predictable] <| Set.Ioc i j ×ˢ s := by

    11  /-!
    12  # Order-closed topologies
    13  
    14  In this file we introduce 3 typeclass mixins that relate topology and order structures:
    15  
    16  - `ClosedIicTopology` says that all the intervals $(-∞, a]$ (formally, `Set.Iic a`)
    17    are closed sets;
    18  - `ClosedIciTopology` says that all the intervals $[a, +∞)$ (formally, `Set.Ici a`)
    19    are closed sets;
    20  - `OrderClosedTopology` says that the set of points `(x, y)` such that `x ≤ y`
    21    is closed in the product topology.
    22  
    23  The last predicate implies the first two.
    24  
    25  We prove many basic properties of such topologies.
    26  
    27  ## Main statements
    28  
    29  This file contains the proofs of the following facts.
    30  For exact requirements
    31  (`OrderClosedTopology` vs `ClosedIciTopology` vs `ClosedIicTopology`,
    32  `Preorder` vs `PartialOrder` vs `LinearOrder`, etc.)
    33  see their statements.
    34  
    35  ### Open / closed sets
    36  
    37  * `isOpen_lt` : if `f` and `g` are continuous functions, then `{x | f x < g x}` is open;
    38  * `isOpen_Iio`, `isOpen_Ioi`, `isOpen_Ioo` : open intervals are open;
    39  * `isClosed_le` : if `f` and `g` are continuous functions, then `{x | f x ≤ g x}` is closed;
    40  * `isClosed_Iic`, `isClosed_Ici`, `isClosed_Icc` : closed intervals are closed;
    41  * `frontier_le_subset_eq`, `frontier_lt_subset_eq` : frontiers of both `{x | f x ≤ g x}`
    42    and `{x | f x < g x}` are included by `{x | f x = g x}`;
    43  
    44  ### Convergence and inequalities
    45  
    46  * `le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto` : if `f` converges to `a`, `g` converges to `b`, and eventually
    47    `f x ≤ g x`, then `a ≤ b`
    48  * `le_of_tendsto`, `ge_of_tendsto` : if `f` converges to `a` and eventually `f x ≤ b`
    49    (resp., `b ≤ f x`), then `a ≤ b` (resp., `b ≤ a`); we also provide primed versions
    50    that assume the inequalities to hold for all `x`.
    51  * `monotone_of_frequently_monotone_of_tendsto`, `antitone_of_frequently_antitone_of_tendsto` : the
    52    pointwise limit of frequently monotone or antitone functions is monotone or antitone.
    53  
    54  ### Min, max, `sSup` and `sInf`
    55  
    56  * `Continuous.min`, `Continuous.max`: pointwise `min`/`max` of two continuous functions is
    57    continuous.
    58  * `Tendsto.min`, `Tendsto.max` : if `f` tends to `a` and `g` tends to `b`, then their pointwise
    59    `min`/`max` tend to `min a b` and `max a b`, respectively.
